prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1206; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim number.

Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was in the parking lot of a shopping center in Sugar Land, Texas. I had just parked near the main entrance and was pulling out of the space.

Q: Which direction were you traveling, and what happened next?

A: I was backing out slowly. The other vehicle was coming down the aisle, and I didn't see it until it was almost on top of me. We hit at the rear quarter panel on my side.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: How fast would you estimate you were moving when you struck or were struck?

A: Maybe three or four miles an hour. It wasn't a hard hit, but it jerked me around in the seat.

Q: Did you feel any injuries right away?

A: Not at first. I felt stiff about an hour later, and by that night my lower back was really sore. I went to urgent care the next morning.

Q: What treatment have you received since then?

A: They diagnosed a back strain and told me to rest, take anti-inflammatories, and do some physical therapy. I've had about six sessions so far, and I'm still having trouble sitting for long periods.

Q: Have you missed any work because of this?

A: I missed two days and I've been on lighter duties since then.

Q: Did you have any prior problems with your back?

A: I had some minor stiffness years ago, but nothing that required treatment or time off.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Just that I want this handled fairly, and I'm willing to provide my medical records.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
